paper.title_en: Isospin effects and symmetry energy in nuclear reactions
paper.abstract_en: Isospin and the symmetry energy are linked within the symmetry term of the liquid-drop mass formula and within the corresponding term of the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter. The Pauli exclusion principle leads to a leading quadratic dependence of the kinetic part of the symmetry term of the nuclear binding-energy formula on the neutron-proton asymmetry (N-Z)/A. Charge symmetry ensures the same leading quadratic dependence for the potential part. Charge invariance further generalizes this dependence, to lowest order, from T$_3^2$ to T(T+1). The strength of the symmetry term, in contrast, is determined by the symmetry energy. At sub-saturation densities the symmetry energy can be constrained by nuclear-structure observables, such as neutron skin thicknesses, isovector collective modes and the related electric dipole polarizability, and excitation energies of isobaric analog states. It can also be constrained by reaction observables, such as charge exchange and elastic scattering cross sections, isoscaling and isospin diffusion. At supra-saturation densities, by contrast, the only means of studying asymmetric nuclear matter under laboratory conditions are relativistic heavy-ion collisions. These studies use differential observables such as neutron/proton flows and light isobar or $π^{-}/π^{+}$ ratios. Complementary information can be obtained from neutron star observations including gravitational waves. The latest measurements and analyses of the stiffness of the symmetry energy will be presented, together with the recent NA61/SHINE observation of an unexpectedly large isospin-symmetry violation in kaon production. Attention will also be paid to the challenges of measuring charged and neutral products of relativistic heavy-ion collisions in the context of the recent ASY-EOS II experiment at GSI and to the new detectors used in the setup.
